verified_against_binary: v2.37.0 implements the Cowork Docs Redesign from the Claude Design project, imported via the design MCP. No fact was changed by the redesign; the wording of every rule, tier, caveat and date is as it was. New layout: a grouped sidebar (Filesystem / Runtime / Extending / Stability), a sticky header carrying the verification stamp and a theme toggle, a symptom-first entry page, per-rule anchors with an on-page contents column, and a contract page that filters, ticks and copies. NEW EDITORIAL AXIS -- severity (silent / loud / friction), answering 'what does this mistake cost' as distinct from the existing confidence tier, which answers 'how do we know'. The 52 assignments come from the design file itself; they are marked editorial rather than measured, rendered in a visually distinct style, and a test asserts the two vocabularies can never collide. Content fix surfaced by the redesign: the entry page claimed SEVEN failure modes and enumerated seven while eight topic pages exist -- the missing one was 'what can change without any version bump', which is the page most likely to matter later. Design fidelity was checked by rendering the built site in a browser rather than by reading markup: the severity filter reports 24 of 52 for SILENT, which matches the data exactly, the theme toggle switches and relabels, and the console is clean.
note: One external dependency is introduced by the design: Google Fonts (Public Sans, JetBrains Mono). Until now the site made no third-party requests. The fonts are render-affecting but not render-blocking (display=swap) and there is a full system-font fallback, so the page is readable before they arrive -- but this is a real change to a site whose other property is being self-contained, and switching to the system stack is a one-line edit if that trade is not wanted.
